text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Container transhipment group ECT will lose Danish shipping line Maersk as customer as Maersk is to build own terminal on the Maasvlakte near Rotterdam. (p1)
- Health minister Els Borst must look for savings as health spending to exceed last September's budget. (p2)
- German DIY shops chain Hornbach to open first of 15 megashops in Netherlands. (p1)
- No panic at Amsterdam Stock Exchange following two successive falls in share prices on Wall Street. (p1)
- Electric power systems maker Holec's general director unexpectantly leaves the company. (p3)
- Software house Management Share hopeful about 1997 after last year's jump in profit. (p3)
- Textile and blinds maker Blydenstein-Willink declines to forecast earnings after higher losses in 1996. (p4)
- Philips Electronics' Hearing Instruments and U.S. company Micro-Tech agree strategic alliance. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Amsterdam Stock Exchange will reconsider opening hours after yesterday's reaction to Wall Street. (p1)
- Asset manager PVF expects further drop in share prices. (p2)
- Cable TV newspaper publishers Wegener Nieuws TV and Holland Advertising Nieuwe Media to closely cooperate. (p2)
- Printer Roto Smeets de Boer to take over rival Plantjn Groep. (p17) DE TELEGRAAF
- Philps Electronics stops sponsoring soccer Champions League because it is too expensive. (p1)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm sees limited tax reduction in 1998, but no extra money for ministries. (p3)
- Friesland Bank takes over participation company Haarlemse Participatie Maatschappij HPM. (p25)
- Malaysia's investment group Khazanach Nasional waits for green light from Malaysian government to take over aircraft maker Fokker.
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Chief of Hungarian insurance unit of ABN Amro bank is accused by rival ING of stealing company secrets. (p1)
- Dutch tourist sector boosts ambitions and seeks better cooperation. (p75)
TROUW
- TV and video sector work on code for violent movies. (p3)
- ABN Amro bank and insurer Nationale Nederlanden raise mortgage rates. (p7)
